Bachelor's Degree in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering, or related fields and/or equivalent experience/training. (Required)
One year minimum of research experience.
Experience using and/or ability to learn software to design DNA constructs and analyze DNA sequences.
Experience in manipulating DNA, transforming bacteria, and culturing bacteria.

The Staff Research Associate 1 participates in a team of scientists and engineers who engineer a bacterium to produce a variety of chemicals. The work will involve high-throughput cloning, optimizing heterologous gene expression in the host bacterium, and analyzing the production of the desired molecules. The chosen individual will focus mainly on cloning and strain construction.
Strain Construction and Development - 25%
The SRA 1 will primarily work on building plasmids and strains to assist in the achievement of the goals of the project.
DNA Design and Planning - 15%
The SRA 1 will assist in the process of designing different DNA builds and strains to meet the project's goals.
Laboratory Operations and Support - 15%
The SRA 1 will assist with other project tasks, such as work with bioreactors, separations, analytics, liquid handlers, etc. to help meet project milestones.
Project Presentation - 10%
The SRA 1 will attend weekly project meetings to present their progress
Project Coordination - 5%
The SRA 1 will attend additional project-specific meetings and sub-group meetings
The SRA 1 will need to utilize the project's electronic lab notebook system to keep track of DNA builds, strains, and data collection.
Laboratory Maintenance - 15%
Maintain a clean lab bench and personal space.
Laboratory Citizenship - 5%
Complete their assigned laboratory citizen job.
Familiarity with analytical equipment (LC/MS, HPLC, GC, ect).
Comfortable with using molecular bio inventory and data management systems.
Ability to work independently in the lab.
